learning_outcomes.text: Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes aspects that imply knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.
Students have developed those learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Students can transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid-mechanical systems and machines.
Ability to work, direct and manage conflicts in a multidisciplinary group and/or a multilingual environment.
Ability to apply new technologies including information and communication technologies.
Ability for information management, handling and application of technical specifications and necessary legislation for engineering practice.
Knowledge of the basic principles of fluid mechanics and their application to problem-solving in the field of engineering. Calculation of pipes, channels, and fluid systems.
Basic knowledge about the use and programming of computers, operating systems, databases, and computer programs with application in engineering.

syllabus_topics: Fluid distribution networks: water supply, fire extinguishing, irrigation, etc.
Analysis of branched networks and meshed networks.
Cavitation and Water hammer.
Gas distribution networks.
Head loss in gases.
Head loss with heat addition.
Application to natural gas transport.
Network calculation using industrial computational tools: introduction to Epanet.
Oleohydraulics and pneumatics.
Instrumentation of fluid installations: flow, pressure, temperature meters.
Study of open channel flow: Specific energy of a channel, Flow under a gate and over a weir, Hydraulic jump.
Brief review of flow in conduits.
Analysis of distribution networks.
Types of networks: branched and meshed networks.
Design of distribution networks.
Transient analysis.
Cavitation and water hammer in water distribution systems.
Introduction to computer-aided water network calculation.
Matrix method for distribution network calculation.
Analysis of distribution networks using commercial codes.
Progressive exercises using a computer.
Gas distribution and supply networks for natural gas.
Applications of gas networks.
Gas movement in conduits: Derivation of conservation laws for compressible flow in slowly varying section conduits.
Ideal gas flow in conduits, convergent-divergent nozzle, shock waves.
Review of open channel flow: specific energy of a channel, flow under a gate and over a weir, and hydraulic jump.
Analytical solution for uniform, non-uniform, gradually and strongly varied flow.
Flow meters.
Pressure meters.
Temperature meters.
Other instrumentation.
Calculation of distribution networks using the matrix method in Matlab (practical).
Calculation of distribution networks using Epanet (practical).
Study of open channel flow: flow around obstacles, hydraulic jump, and flow through a gate (practical).
teaching_methods: Exposition of theory and general examples
Small group classes in computer labs
Problem-solving sessions using commercial software (Epanet and Matlab)
Experimental practices in fluid mechanics laboratory and open channel flows

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and/or participation in face-to-face and/or virtual activities
Written exam on theoretical and practical concepts
Completion and submission of assignments, cases or exercises
Attendance and evaluation of laboratory/field/ICT tool usage practices

assessment_rules: The grading system will be governed by RD 1125/2003 of September 5. To pass the subject, it is essential to obtain a grade equal to or greater than 5 out of 10 in the written exam. Attendance and evaluation of practices will be carried out by attendance control and submission of a report with the solution to the problems posed. Several assignments will be proposed, which will be presented and defended in class. The rest of the grade corresponds to student attendance and participation.
